mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from a recent trough, weekday trip chaining raises discretionary shopping within four weeks. The mechanism is a return-to-office effect: more commuting creates more lunchtime and after-work retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC after a short lag.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES turns positive after at least one week below 0
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -14.9 to -0.6 while TRANSIT stayed below baseline in the latest week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains near or below baseline but RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 28 days, the commuting-driven uplift is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in TRANSIT suppresses spontaneous shopping because fewer riders pass retail corridors and malls. When transit mobility stays negative for multiple weeks, RETAIL_REC should fall within one to two weeks and remain weak over the month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below 0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is negative in t-2w, t-1w, and t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains negative for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC does not weaken within the next 14 days, the transit-exposure channel fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays very high while RETAIL_REC falls, households are concentrating trips on essentials and deferring discretionary purchases. This substitution should keep retail-and-recreation mobility below the prior four-week average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 45 while RETAIL_REC is below 0
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is near 49-54 across all weeks while RETAIL_REC fell to -13.3
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above 45 and RETAIL_REC still rises above its last-four-week mean over the next 28 days, the essentials-substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility signals reduced leisure outings and lower overall out-of-home activity. That leisure pullback typically spills into malls and restaurants with a one-week lag, pushing RETAIL_REC downward in the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -4.4 to -16.7 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS drops more than 5 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following 7 days, the leisure-spillover claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are suppressed together, the city is in a mobility-constrained regime that depresses discretionary retail demand. The joint contraction should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average for the next two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT < 0 and WORKPLACES < 0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is negative in t-1w and t-0w while WORKPLACES is near zero to negative in the latest week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both negative but RETAIL_REC recovers above its last-four-week mean within 28 days, the constrained-mobility mechanism is false.

mechanism_narrative: A high RESIDENTIAL reading indicates people are staying home more, which reduces discretionary store visits with a short lag. If residential mobility stays elevated, RETAIL_REC should continue falling over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 6 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 9.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 6 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next 14 days, the stay-home dampening channel is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Retail mobility falls when falling TRANSIT coincides with rising RESIDENTIAL, because commuters are replaced by stay-at-home behavior. The interaction should matter more than either series alone and produce a negative RETAIL_REC change within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is negative in the latest two weeks while RESIDENTIAL is above baseline
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below baseline and RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior four weeks over the next 28 days, the interaction mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stops recovering and turns negative again after a brief rebound, it indicates renewed activity restraint that will spill into fewer shopping trips. The effect should appear within one week and persist across the month unless workplace mobility resumes strongly.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses from positive to negative week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from 6.0 to -0.6 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES crosses back below 0 but RETAIL_REC does not weaken in the next 7 days, the renewed-restraint mechanism is rejected.
